summary:
H.E.L.I.O.S. is an autonomous astronaut health-monitoring and decision-support system developed to protect crew health during long-duration space missions. With communication delays of up to 24 minutes between Earth and Mars, astronauts need reliable onboard technology to independently monitor their health and respond to emergencies.

HELIOS integrates real-time physiological, environmental, radiation, activity, sleep, and laboratory data into one intelligent platform. It tracks vital signs, compares health metrics against individual baselines using NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) datasets, and identifies potential risks before they become critical. Its AI assistant, Helix-AI Analyst, interprets medical data and delivers clear voice alerts through four severity levels: NOMINAL, WATCH, WARNING, and CRITICAL.

For spacewalks and lunar or Martian surface missions, HELIOS provides an augmented-reality helmet display showing vital signs, spacesuit conditions, oxygen reserves, radiation exposure, and navigation guidance. It also synchronizes mission data with Earth-based Mission Control while accounting for communication delays.

HELIOS is important because it bridges the gap between astronauts and Earth-based medical support, enabling faster, informed decisions and greater crew autonomy. By combining continuous monitoring, AI-driven analysis, and real-time guidance, it helps reduce health risks and protect human life in deep-space exploration.
details:
We Solved Astronauts Health Monitoring Software For Deep Space Missions By HELIOS.
H.E.L.I.O.S. is an autonomous astronaut health-monitoring and decision-support system designed for long-duration space missions. Beyond Earth, communication delays of up to 24 minutes to Mars make immediate support from Mission Control impossible. Astronauts therefore need reliable onboard systems to monitor and manage their health independently.

Github Link Of Our Project: https://github.com/aero-vitals/H.E.L.I.O.S

Highlighted Features:

  • Autonomous onboard health monitoring
  • AI-powered health analysis and decision support
  • Real-time anomaly detection and risk assessment
  • Independent operation during communication delays
  • SUIT HUD

Data We Used:

HELIOS integrates real-time physiological, environmental, radiation, activity, sleep, and laboratory data into one intelligent platform. It continuously monitors vital signs, including ECG, heart rate, oxygen levels, respiratory rate, body temperature, and spacecraft environmental conditions. Health data is also compared against individual baselines using NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) datasets.

When abnormalities are detected, HELIOS identifies potential health risks, assesses their severity, and provides recommended countermeasures before conditions become critical.

At its core, Helix-AI Analyst acts as an onboard AI health assistant, translating complex medical data into clear voice alerts. Its alert system uses four levels: NOMINAL, WATCH, WARNING, and CRITICAL, helping astronauts quickly understand their health status.

During spacewalks and lunar or Martian surface missions, HELIOS displays essential health and spacesuit information through an augmented-reality helmet HUD, including vital signs, oxygen reserves, suit pressure, radiation exposure, and navigation guidance.

HELIOS also synchronizes mission data with Earth-based Mission Control, accounting for realistic communication delays while maintaining independent onboard monitoring and decision support.

HELIOS does not replace astronauts or Mission Control. It empowers crews with the intelligence and tools needed to make informed health decisions, respond to emergencies, and protect human life during deep-space exploration.

Our Journey:

What started as an idea became an incredible journey of innovation, teamwork, and discovery. As Team AeroVitals, we challenged ourselves to build HELIOS, bringing AI and space science together to make deep-space exploration safer.

From brainstorming to building our prototype, every challenge taught us something new. We learned, experimented, collaborated, and pushed beyond our limits.

More than just a competition, NASA Space Apps was an opportunity to grow, think differently, and turn imagination into innovation.

Grateful to NASA for making this journey possible.
